title: The Washing Away of Wrongs (Xiyuan jilu)
summary: Song Ci wrote the Xiyuan jilu, also called The Washing Away of Wrongs, in 1247 during the Southern Song. It is described as the first known forensic handbook, aimed at local coroners, covering topics such as autopsy and distinguishing murder from suicide. Song Ci came from a bureaucratic family in Jianyang, Fujian, and worked as a senior criminal judge.

uncertainty.note: Two sources give 1247 for the writing; other accounts of publication are not cited.

where.modern_name: Jianyang District, Nanping, Fujian, China (author's family home; labelled proxy pin, place of writing not stated)

importance.justification: Described as the first known forensic handbook and the earliest systematic book on judicial examination (Mutter Museum; China Daily).
